items.title: A flat finite module over a polynomial ring that is finitely presented at finitely many primes is finitely presented
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a finite flat module over a polynomial ring is finitely presented as soon as it is finitely presented at finitely many primes which detect the base by the injectivity of the map to the product of localisations, and the proof is a 31-line argument combining openness of flatness with a diagram. It presents the module, finds finitely many elements of the kernel that generate it after localising at the chosen primes and at a given prime of the polynomial ring, forms the resulting quotient module, uses openness of flatness to localise so that this quotient is flat, and then compares the two flat modules through the product of localisations to conclude that the surjection between them is injective. The two inputs that do the work are the openness theorem and the injectivity hypothesis on the base, and both are used explicitly.
